entities.summary:
The assassination of Julius Caesar, which took place on March 15, 44 BCE, in the Theatre of Pompey, marked a pivotal moment in Roman history. 

This event was significant due to its impact on the Roman Republic, as it led to a power vacuum and eventually the rise of the Roman Empire under Augustus Caesar. 

The assassination was carried out by a group of senators, including Marcus Junius Brutus and Gaius Cassius Longinus, who were motivated by a desire to restore the Roman Republic and end Julius Caesar's authoritarian rule. 

The consequences of the assassination were far-reaching, as it led to a period of civil war and ultimately the rise of the Roman Empire.

As Cicero noted, 'The murder of Julius Caesar was a crime, but it was also a turning point in the history of Rome.'
